source_title: Ras Al Khaimah targets threefold visitor growth as hotel pipeline expands - ET TravelWorld
source_excerpt: Ras Al Khaimah is looking to convert the resilience demonstrated during a turbulent year for international travel into a more ambitious phase of tourism growth, with India emerging as a key market and a significant expansion of its hospitality offering set to broaden the emirate’s appeal.Speaking to ET TravelWorld on the sidelines of Arabian Travel Market 2026, Iyad Rasbey, Vice President, Destination Tourism Development at Ras Al Khaimah Tourism Development Authority (RAKTDA), said the emirate had started the year strongly before regional conflict prompted a shift towards the domestic market. The strategy helped sustain tourism activity and keep hotels operating while international travel flows were affected.The emirate welcomed more than 670,000 visitors in the first half of 2026, its strongest first-half performance on record, according to RAKTDA. Domestic arrivals rose 47% year on year, with May recording the destination’s strongest monthly performance.For Rasbey, the experience reinforced the importance of market diversification and the domestic market’s role in supporting the tourism ecosystem through periods of uncertainty.India remains central to the recoveryIndia continues to rank among Ras Al Khaimah’s top five source markets, with growth supported by connectivity, destination awareness and demand from MICE groups, Rasbey said.He pointed to 14% year-on-year growth in Indian visitor arrivals in 2025 and said the market had continued to perform well in 2026, despite the challenging environment. In the interview, he cited growth of around 27% for May. A subsequent RAKTDA update reported that Indian arrivals from May 2026 onwards had risen 30% year on year, alongside a 12% increase in room revenue.Connectivity remains an important part of that equation. Direct flights operated by IndiGo, Air India Express and Air Arabia serve multiple Indian touchpoints, while Dubai International Airport provides another access route, approximately 45 minutes from the emirate, according to RAKTDA. The authority has also signed a memorandum of understanding with Emirates covering joint marketing, trade and media familiarisation programmes, tailored products and packages, and trade incentives in selected markets.Beyond air access, Rasbey highlighted the role of destination marketing and MICE business in bringing Indian travellers to the emirate. India’s potential, he suggested, extends beyond conventional leisure travel to group movements, corporate events and celebrations.MICE and weddings offer room to growRas Al Khaimah is looking to build on its presence in India’s MICE and destination wedding segments, both of which stand to benefit from the emirate’s expanding hotel inventory and events infrastructure.Rasbey said the destination had recorded 25% year-on-year growth in MICE revenue in 2025. While momentum had slowed amid the wider disruption, he remained optimistic about India’s contribution to future growth.The hotel pipeline is expected to add capacity and give planners more options across different budgets, group sizes and event formats. Rotana Ras Al Khaimah – The Mangroves, a 258-room property with a large ballroom, ten meeting rooms and an outdoor events space, is positioned to strengthen the emirate’s MICE and wedding offering. SAIJ Mountain Lodge by Mantis, the first mountain lodge on Jebel Jais, is expected to add a more nature-led proposition centred on wellness and outdoor experiences.For Indian wedding planners, the proposition is not limited to beachfront venues. The emirate’s combination of beaches, mountains, desert landscapes and resorts allows it to cater to different celebration styles, while additional accommodation and event facilities could increase its capacity to host larger or more varied gatherings.Wynn and the next phase of destination developmentThe most prominent addition to Ras Al Khaimah’s tourism landscape is Wynn Al Marjan Island, scheduled to open in September 2027. The development is expected to bring 1,530 rooms, suites and villas, alongside dining, entertainment, retail and event offerings.Rasbey described the project as a significant addition to the destination’s evolving proposition, but stressed that it would be part of a broader wave of development rather than a standalone growth driver. Several new hotels and experiences are expected to expand the range of options available to visitors over the coming years.The broader challenge will be to translate new supply into sustained demand, particularly across different seasons and source markets. RAKTDA’s stated Tourism Vision 2030 is to attract more than 3.5 million annual visitors while building an industry that is economically, environmentally and socially sustainable.A clearer identity for a diverse destinationAlongside the physical expansion, RAKTDA is working on a repositioning of the destination brand, which Rasbey said would be launched soon. The aim is to communicate more clearly what Ras Al Khaimah stands for without narrowing its appeal to a single travel segment.The emirate’s current offer spans family holidays, romantic escapes, adventure, nature and cultural experiences. Rasbey said the challenge was to retain that breadth while developing an identity that international travellers could readily understand.That distinction matters as destinations across the region compete to attract travellers with new hotels, attractions and premium experiences. Ras Al Khaimah’s proposition has traditionally drawn on its mix of coastline, desert, mountains and heritage; the forthcoming repositioning is intended to bring greater coherence to how that diversity is presented to the market.The emirate’s official strategy similarly emphasises sustainable, nature-based adventure and authentic cultural experiences as differentiators in an increasingly competitive tourism landscape.Doubling inventory, tripling visitorsLooking ahead, Rasbey outlined an ambitious growth trajectory: doubling the emirate’s current hotel inventory over the next few years and tripling visitor numbers over the next four to five years.Achieving that scale will require more than adding rooms. Air access, experiences, events, destination awareness and demand generation will need to develop in tandem, while the emirate retains the mix of leisure and nature-led experiences that distinguishes it from more established regional destinations.For India, the opportunity is to convert growing awareness and connectivity into more consistent demand across leisure, MICE and weddings. For Ras Al Khaimah, the next phase will test whether investment in new hospitality assets and a sharper destination identity can turn recent resilience into sustained international growth.
